spec: Given a list of (a, b) integer tuples, return them sorted by the sum a + b in ascending order. If two tuples have the same sum, order by the first element a ascending. The input list may be empty.
Return a new string consisting of only the characters at even zero-based indices (0, 2, 4, ...) of the input string, preserving their relative order. An empty string returns an empty string.

Given an integer day number, where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively (day_number % 7 gives the weekday, 5=Saturday, 6=Sunday), return the smallest day number that is greater than or equal to the given one and falls on a weekday (Monday-Friday).

Write a function that combines three lists element by index into a list of triples (a[i], b[i], c[i]). If the lists have different lengths, stop at the length of the shortest list. Return an empty list if the shortest input is empty.

Validate a Sudoku row: a list of exactly 9 integers where 0 represents an empty cell. Every non-zero value must be between 1 and 9 (inclusive) and no non-zero value may repeat within the row. Return False if the list is not length 9, contains an out-of-range value, or has a duplicate non-zero value.

Write a function that removes from a list every element that is None, or that is a string, list, tuple, or dict with zero length, while keeping all other values (including 0, 0.0, and False) and preserving order. The input list may contain a mix of types and may be empty.

Given a date as (year, month, day) integers and an integer number of months n (which may be negative), return the (year, month, day) tuple after adding n months to the month/year, clamping the day to the last valid day of the resulting month if necessary (e.g. adding 1 month to January 31 gives February 28 or 29).

Bucket the integers in nums into fixed-width bins of size bin_size (a positive integer), where a number's bin is identified by its floor-divided lower bound (num // bin_size * bin_size). Return a dict mapping each occupied bin's lower bound to the count of numbers in it. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Write a function that splits a list of numbers into two parts at the position of the first zero: everything before it, and everything from it onward (inclusive). Return the two parts as a tuple (before, from_zero_onward). If there is no zero in the list, return the whole list as the first part and an empty list as the second.

Given a string of whitespace-separated words, form an acronym by taking the first letter of each word, converting it to uppercase, and concatenating the letters together with no separators. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty string.
Given a paragraph made of sentences separated by '. ' (period then space), capitalize the first letter of each sentence and rejoin them with '. '.
visible_tests: assert capitalize_sentences('hello world. this is a test.') == 'Hello world. This is a test.'
assert capitalize_sentences('one sentence only') == 'One sentence only'
assert capitalize_sentences('first. second. third.') == 'First. Second. Third.'

spec: Merge two dicts into one containing all keys from both. When a key appears in both, the value from d2 is kept. Return the merged dict without modifying the inputs.

Given a string s, consider only its digit characters in order (ignoring all non-digit characters, which do not break adjacency between digits) and count the number of adjacent digit pairs where the second digit is strictly greater than the first. A string with fewer than two digits returns 0.

Given a list of dictionaries each with a 'name' key and a 'tags' key holding a list, sort the records ascending by the number of tags. Ties are broken by name ascending. An empty list returns an empty list.

Validate a string that must contain only the characters '[' and ']'. Return True if the square brackets are balanced (properly nested, equal counts, never more closes than opens at any point) and no other character appears; otherwise return False.

Given a list of non-negative integers, return them sorted by the product of their decimal digits, ascending (a digit of 0 makes the product 0). If two numbers have the same digit product, order them by value ascending. The input list may be empty.

Write a function that takes a list of numbers and a window size k, and computes the average of every contiguous window of k consecutive elements, rounding each average to the nearest integer using standard Python rounding. Return the list of rounded averages in order, one per window. Return an empty list if k is less than or equal to 0 or k is greater than the length of the list.

Given a string of lowercase letters, determine whether it can become a palindrome by removing at most one character. Return True if the string is already a palindrome, or becomes one after deleting exactly one character (checked by a standard two-pointer approach with a single allowed mismatch skip), otherwise False.
Write a function that computes the arithmetic mean of a non-empty list of numbers and counts how many elements are strictly greater than that mean. Return the count as an integer.

Given a list of integers, return True if each element is strictly greater than the next (no equal adjacent values allowed), and False otherwise. An empty list or a single-element list is considered strictly sorted.
Given a dict whose values are either plain values or further nested dicts, count the total number of leaf values (non-dict values) anywhere in the structure, recursively. An empty dict returns 0.
Convert a snake_case string (words separated by underscores) into PascalCase, capitalizing every word and removing the underscores.

Given a list of items and a permutation perm of indices of the same length, return a new list result such that result[perm[i]] equals items[i] for every i. This effectively undoes the reordering that perm would apply. An empty items list with an empty permutation returns an empty list.

Given a sorted list of integer boundaries, assign each number in nums to a bucket index equal to the count of boundaries that are less than or equal to it (so numbers below all boundaries get bucket 0, and numbers at or above the last boundary get the highest bucket index). Return a dict mapping each occupied bucket index to the count of numbers in it. An empty nums list returns an empty dict.

If a filename ends with the same non-empty extension repeated twice in a row, separated by periods (for example 'file.tar.tar'), remove one of the two duplicate trailing extensions so it appears only once (giving 'file.tar'). If the filename does not end this way, return it unchanged.

Determine whether a string fully matches a wildcard pattern, where '?' in the pattern matches any single character and '*' matches any sequence of characters (including an empty sequence). All other characters in the pattern must match themselves exactly.

Convert a date given as (year, month, day) to its ordinal day count in the proleptic Gregorian calendar, where day 1 corresponds to January 1st of year 1. Assume the date is valid and year is a positive integer.

Given a list of strings and a positive integer n (at most the number of distinct strings), return the n most frequent strings ordered from most frequent to least frequent. If two strings occur the same number of times, order them alphabetically ascending.

Given two numeric amounts low and high, format each as a dollar string with thousands separators and two decimal places, and combine them as 'low-high' separated by a hyphen, for example '$10.00-$20.00'.
Given a year and month, determine whether the 13th day of that month falls on a Friday, using Zeller's congruence. Return True or False.

Given two strings a and b, return the length of the longest common prefix they share (the number of leading characters that match exactly, case-sensitive). Return 0 if they share no common prefix or if either string is empty.

Write a function that shifts the elements of a list to the left by n positions, dropping the first n elements and filling the last n positions with a given fill value; the result has the same length as the input. If n is 0 or negative, return a copy of the list unchanged; if n is at least the length of the list, return a list of the fill value repeated to the original length.

Determine whether (year, month, day) forms a valid Gregorian calendar date, where year must be a positive integer, month between 1 and 12, and day between 1 and the number of days in that month for that year (accounting for leap years). Return True or False.

Write a function that splits a list into consecutive chunks of a given size k, returning a list of chunks. The last chunk may contain fewer than k elements if the list length is not a multiple of k. Assume k is a positive integer; the input list may be empty.

Given a list of (group, item) tuples, determine for each group how many distinct items it contains (duplicates within the same group counted once). Return a dict mapping each group to its distinct item count. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a non-empty list of integers, compute its median (using the odd/even averaging rule), then return the values sorted by their absolute difference from that median, ascending. If two values have the same absolute difference, the smaller value comes first.

Count the number of distinct words in a string of whitespace-separated words, treating words that differ only in letter case as the same word. An empty or whitespace-only string has zero distinct words.
Return a new string in which every character of the input string is duplicated (appears twice in a row), preserving the original order. An empty string returns an empty string.

Given two dates d1 and d2, each a (year, month, day) tuple with d2 on or after d1, return the number of whole months elapsed from d1 to d2: the difference in (year*12 + month), reduced by one if d2's day-of-month is earlier than d1's.
Compute the sum of the proper divisors of a positive integer n, i.e. all positive divisors of n strictly less than n (this sum is 0 for n = 1).
